title: What Food Resilience Networks Is
definition: Food Resilience Networks: networks feeding cities in shocks.
description:

t: Real Research Today: Food Resilience Networks
title: Real Research Today: Food Resilience Networks
definition: Today's documented research behind Food Resilience Networks.
description:
The road to Food Resilience Networks is already being paved. The Svalbard Global Seed Vault and Arctic World Archive back up seeds and data. NASA's DART mission (2022) successfully deflected the asteroid Dimorphos, proving planetary defense.

Mesh-network emergency comms (goTenna, Serval heritage) keep responders connected off-grid. Together these programs form the food hubs foundation that Food Resilience Networks will build on — the network logistics results, the stock rotation methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as network logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Food Resilience Networks
definition: Estimates Food Resilience Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Food Resilience Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Food Resilience Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Food Resilience Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 97453 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where food hubs monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or stock rotation maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Food Resilience Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Food Resilience Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Food Resilience Networks — networks feeding cities in shocks.

Phase 1 — Prove (food hubs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (stock rotation): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (last-mile): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and cities-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
